tasks.source_question:
You are given two tables and the code that turns them into model inputs, from a heavy-chain CDR engineering campaign for a therapeutic antibody. `training_library_binding.csv` has 4,000 heavy-chain variants from a sorted display library, each with a measured antigen-binding class label and a measured off-target (ovalbumin) binding class label -- the data used to fit two linear discriminant (LDA) models, one per property, on a one-hot encoding of the full heavy-chain variable-domain sequence. `onehot_gen.py` is the actual encoding function those models were built on. `igg_binding.csv` is a 96-variant held-out soluble-IgG panel that includes the unmutated background sequence, several already-engineered leads, and a `Blosum62` flag marking the subset the researchers specifically built to test whether the fitted models say anything useful about CDR positions the 4,000-variant library never touched.

The researchers' own write-up describes these one-hot models as "insensitive to variation at novel sites in the CDRs ... because they are defined based on the sequences of the antibody mutants in the library."

Within the `Blosum62`-flagged rows of the held-out panel, some variants carry an added mutation at a CDR position genuinely outside the eight positions the library was built to vary; others differ from the unmutated background only by a new combination of residues at those same eight positions. Nothing in the table names which is which -- that has to come from comparing each sequence against the panel's own unmutated background entry.

For every flagged variant that does carry a mutation at a position genuinely outside those eight, determine which ones the fitted antigen-binding model can be trusted to say anything real about, versus which should be treated as no more informative than the unmutated background's own prediction when deciding whether to advance them. Then, restricted to that same full group of flagged variants carrying a mutation outside those eight positions, determine whether the model's population-level correlation with measured antigen binding is statistically real, and separately whether its correlation with measured off-target binding is statistically real. Report the exact set of variants that population draws from.

Separately, report how many of the 4,000 library sequences carry a residue substitution at a position outside the eight the library was designed to vary.

Return EXACTLY:

<EVAL_ANSWER>
{"informative_candidates": ["<Sample id>", "..."], "correlation_population": ["<Sample id>", "..."], "affinity_significant": <true|false>, "specificity_significant": <true|false>, "n_incidental_training_clones": <integer>}
</EVAL_ANSWER>

- informative_candidates: the `Sample` values (exactly as they appear in `igg_binding.csv`) of the genuinely-novel-site variants whose antigen-binding model score you would treat as real evidence.
- correlation_population: the `Sample` values (exactly as they appear in `igg_binding.csv`) of every genuinely-novel-site variant you actually included when computing both correlations below.
- affinity_significant / specificity_significant: whether the model's correlation with measured antigen binding, and separately with measured off-target binding, restricted to that same genuinely-novel-site group, clears ordinary statistical significance.
- n_incidental_training_clones: how many of the 4,000 training-library sequences carry a substitution at a position outside the eight the library was designed to vary.

tasks.source_question:
A synapse-classification model was trained entirely on images from one T-cell-triggering stimulus, then applied to score synapse images collected under a second, mechanistically different T-cell-triggering stimulus. The only check on record for whether the model's calls still mean the same thing under the new stimulus is one additional expert's review of images from each of two antibody conditions, scored against the model's own predictions: macro-F1 = 0.86 on the first condition (396 images) and 0.85 on the second (227 images). Those figures are reported as confirming that the model generalizes across the switch in stimulus, and are being used to support treating the classifier's synapse-class frequency output as mode-of-action evidence ahead of a program decision on a candidate antibody.

Attached is data from two separate re-annotation exercises the modeling team ran on its own original training-condition benchmark images (the stimulus the model was actually trained and tested on, not either antibody condition): a held-out panel independently re-annotated by four raters, for which the model's own per-image label and prediction are also available (first_round.csv, inter-rater-first-round.csv), and a second, non-overlapping panel independently re-annotated by five raters together with its own original consensus label (inter-rater-second-round.csv) -- no model predictions exist for this second panel.

How much weight should the reported 0.85/0.86 concordance carry as evidence that the classifier's calls still mean the same thing under the new stimulus?

Return EXACTLY:

<EVAL_ANSWER>
{"validity_assessment": "<sufficient_confirms_generalization|insufficient_confirmed_mechanism_driven_degradation|insufficient_underpowered_single_rater_check>", "same_mechanism_baseline_sources": ["<first identifier>", "<second identifier>"]}
</EVAL_ANSWER>

validity_assessment is your overall judgment of whether the reported concordance is adequate support for the mode-of-action use case, and if not, which of the two ways it falls short.

tasks.source_question:
A CNS-shuttle programme profiled three independently engineered, species-cross-reactive bispecific antibody candidates (Shuttle-1, Shuttle-2, Shuttle-3) alongside a non-targeting IgG control in a single-dose wild-type mouse study (20 nmol/kg, intravenous). Protein was labelled with 125I by a direct, Pierce-type electrophilic (chloramine-T-style) iodination on tyrosine residues before dosing. Tissue was sampled by gamma counting at 1 hour, 1 day and 7 days post-dose across seven organs (Lung, Liver, Kidney, Heart, Spleen, Brain, Blood), with 3-4 replicate animals per (arm, organ, timepoint) combination, reported as percent injected dose per gram (%ID/g). The three shuttles' shared target, CD98hc, is expressed on brain endothelium as well as on peripheral tissue that includes kidney and spleen.

The programme's translational lead must choose a single shuttle candidate to advance into further development on brain-durability grounds, and decide whether this dataset supports committing to a once-weekly (or less frequent) dosing interval for what would be a brain-resident biologic.

From the delivered biodistribution data alone, determine which shuttle (if any) is defensibly supported as the advancement pick on brain-durability grounds, what dosing-interval commitment (if any) the dataset supports for that pick, and, if the package falls short of a clean recommendation, what specifically limits the conclusion.

You must show the specific per-shuttle readouts your recommendation rests on. Report each shuttle's own observed mean 7-day Brain %ID/g value exactly as computed from the delivered biodistribution data -- this is a direct data readout, required regardless of which recommendation you reach, not a value you can derive from the study description alone.

Return EXACTLY:

<EVAL_ANSWER>
{"recommendation": {"recommended_shuttle": "<Shuttle-1|Shuttle-2|Shuttle-3|INDETERMINATE>", "dosing_interval_supported": "<WEEKLY|LONGER_THAN_WEEKLY|NOT_SUPPORTED>"}, "limiting_factor": "<NON_RESIDUALIZING_LABEL_BIAS|SMALL_SAMPLE_SIZE_AND_BIOLOGICAL_VARIABILITY|NONE_IDENTIFIED>", "brain_7d_shuttle1_pct_id_g": <observed mean 7-day Brain %ID/g for Shuttle-1>, "brain_7d_shuttle2_pct_id_g": <observed mean 7-day Brain %ID/g for Shuttle-2>, "brain_7d_shuttle3_pct_id_g": <observed mean 7-day Brain %ID/g for Shuttle-3>}
</EVAL_ANSWER>

`recommended_shuttle` is your pick among the three named shuttles, or INDETERMINATE if the data does not support choosing one. `dosing_interval_supported` states the longest defensible dosing interval this package supports for the shuttle you name, or NOT_SUPPORTED if no interval commitment is defensible. `limiting_factor` names the single best-supported reason the package falls short of full support for a clean recommendation -- NON_RESIDUALIZING_LABEL_BIAS if the radiolabelling chemistry itself is what limits the conclusion, SMALL_SAMPLE_SIZE_AND_BIOLOGICAL_VARIABILITY if ordinary replicate/animal variability is the limiting concern instead, or NONE_IDENTIFIED if you judge the package fully sufficient for a clean pick. `brain_7d_shuttle1_pct_id_g`, `brain_7d_shuttle2_pct_id_g` and `brain_7d_shuttle3_pct_id_g` are the three shuttles' own observed mean 7-day Brain %ID/g values, read directly off the delivered data -- report the real numbers for all three regardless of which shuttle (if any) you recommend.

A blood-brain-barrier (BBB) delivery program is comparing two non-targeted, bispecific IgG shuttle candidates head-to-head. Both candidates carry the identical non-targeted antibody payload; they differ only in which cerebrovascular target they engage to cross the BBB -- one engages CD98hc, the other engages the transferrin receptor (TfR-1). This is an antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) linker-selection decision; the payload is a DNA-intercalating agent acting on genomic DNA. For five coded linkers (DL-1..DL-5) on two coded carriers (Carrier-X, Carrier-Y), nothing is precomputed: you have per-cell payload intensity in a nuclear and a cytoplasmic region plus each carrier's internalization movie. One linker gives by far the strongest signal. Decide whether to advance it, whether its delivery tracks carrier uptake, and how delivery should be judged.

# Return schema
lead_call_class: 1 advance it; 2 do not; 3 advance a different linker; 4 highest per carrier; 5 insufficient.
uptake_delivery_relationship_class: 1 delivery increases with carrier uptake; 2 delivery does not track carrier uptake; 3 cannot be determined.
basis_class: 1 total payload per cell; 2 nuclear fraction; 3 delivery vs each carrier's internalization.

Return EXACTLY:

tasks.source_question:
You are supporting a dose-finding stage of an oncostatin M neutralising antibody programme, which has to commit in advance to the readout or readouts its dose decision will be read on. The readouts available to it are the ones already collected in the completed repeat-dose study supplied here.

Work from the supplied material. Decide which of the readouts reported there could carry a dose-selection decision, name the readout you would place last for that purpose, and state the rule you would apply. Report, for the readout you place last, what it reads in the higher antibody arm at the final scheduled post-dose visit and at how many post-dose visits it reads the same in both antibody arms. State separately the visits at which you would read the dose decision, the efficacy signal, and the top of the dose range. Report also, as the fitted model has it, how many times longer the slower of the two blood cell lineages this antibody perturbs takes to settle to a new level than the faster one does.

Supplied:
- clinical_study_posted_results.json: the posted results record of the completed repeat-dose study, reported arm by arm and visit by visit.
- haematopoiesis_population_model.mod: a fitted population model control stream covering antibody disposition, ligand turnover and blood cell production.

Report a single flat JSON object.

<EVAL_ANSWER>
{
  "dose_selection_readouts": ["<label>"],
  "least_fit_readout": "<label>",
  "least_fit_readout_final_visit_value": <number>,
  "least_fit_readout_visits_reading_alike_in_both_antibody_arms": <integer>,
  "decision_rule": "<one or two sentences>",
  "dose_selection_visit_day": <integer>,
  "efficacy_visit_day": <integer>,
  "dose_ceiling_visit_day": <integer>,
  "slower_lineage_settling_time_multiple": <number>
}
</EVAL_ANSWER>

Fields:
- dose_selection_readouts: one to three distinct labels, the readouts you would select doses on at the visit you nominate below.
- least_fit_readout: one label, the readout that is least fit to carry a dose-selection decision at any post-dose visit.
- least_fit_readout_final_visit_value: what that readout reports for the higher antibody arm at the last scheduled post-dose visit, in the unit the record reports it in.
- least_fit_readout_visits_reading_alike_in_both_antibody_arms: the number of post-dose visits at which that readout reports the same value for both antibody arms.
- decision_rule: the rule you would apply to the readouts you nominated.
- dose_selection_visit_day: the study day of the visit at which you would read the dose decision.
- efficacy_visit_day: the study day at which you would read the efficacy signal.
- dose_ceiling_visit_day: the study day by which the top of the dose range could be claimed to have been characterised.
- slower_lineage_settling_time_multiple: how many times longer the slower of the two blood cell lineages this antibody perturbs takes to settle to a new level than the faster one does, as the fitted model has it.
